gloss: to embezzle; to become skilled at using

definitions.explanation: to use money or funds entrusted to one for personal purposes; to misuse funds

definitions.gloss: to become skilled at using; to break in
definitions.explanation: to use something repeatedly until it becomes familiar and comfortable, or until one becomes proficient with it

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{金|かね}を{使|つか}い{込|こ}んだ。
{遺産|いさん}を{使|つか}い{込|こ}んでしまった。
この{道具|どうぐ}は{使|つか}い{込|こ}むほど{味|あじ}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: This tool develops more character the more you use it.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{込|こ}まれた{革|かわ}の{財布|さいふ}は{独特|どくとく}の{風合|ふうあ}いがある。
examples.english: A well-used leather wallet has a unique patina.

notes:
{使|つか}い{込|こ}む has two distinct meanings.

SENSE 1 - EMBEZZLEMENT:
- Using funds that belong to others for personal purposes
- Often appears in news about financial crimes
- Related to {横領|おうりょう} (embezzlement)

SENSE 2 - WEARING IN:
- Using something until it becomes comfortable or shows character
- Positive connotation: appreciation for well-used items
- Common with leather goods, tools, musical instruments

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
Sense 1:
- {公金|こうきん}を{使|つか}い{込|こ}む (to embezzle public funds)
- {会社|かいしゃ}の{金|かね}を{使|つか}い{込|こ}む (to embezzle company money)

Sense 2:
- {使|つか}い{込|こ}まれた～ (well-used ~)
- {使|つか}い{込|こ}むほど (the more you use it)

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb. Takes を for money/items.

RELATED TERMS:
- {使|つか}い{果|は}たす (to use up completely)
- {使|つか}い{慣|な}れる (to become accustomed to using)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in both news and everyday contexts.
